mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a UNRATE increase > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which boosts related industries and increases overall economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances following a sustained increase in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% in a single month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to increased prices and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances following a significant decrease in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in 1 quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following RSAFS growth exceeding GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase & UNRATE decrease over 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances following the described labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months, coupled with a stable or decreasing federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS), signals inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, which can lead to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increase & stable/decreasing FEDFUNDS over 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following the described inflationary conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a single month, coupled with a stable or decreasing federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS), signals deflationary pressure without monetary tightening, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decrease > 0.5% & stable/decreasing FEDFUNDS in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances following the described deflationary conditions.
